items.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: Vernon Alley put a little group together with Wardell in it and Gerald Wiggins. Yeah. Wiggins had gotten out of the service. Gerald Wiggins and Wyatt Ruther, Bull Ruther, the bass player... He had this quartet.

ctx.x: Yeah. So he used to come in to Jenkins to listen to us. So one time we did — Ernie knew who he was, I didn’t. Because that was very, very early. But anyhow once we found out who he was then — I don’t know how long he was here because we were at Jenkins maybe for about three months or maybe even longer. So then that job ended so then Ernie said, “Well, Earl, I think it’s time for me to go back to Los Angeles.” His brother Marshall was there and Marshall recorded with Eddie Heywood and traveled with Eddie Heywood’s…

John Kirby’s small band, they brought in Jack McVea and they brought in Eckstine’s big band with Art Blakey and all those cats and I got to see that. They brought in Fatha Hines and I’d go down there on a regular basis, never dreaming that someday that our paths would cross musically. But who was in that band: Wardell Gray was in the band, Kermit Scott, who you’ll see on some of the early Billie Holiday records, Kermit Scott the tenor player. And they both left the band while it was here and so they got who else?…
